Employment and autism

In the United Kingdom, the 2024 Buckland Review stated that only around 3 in 10 autistic people of working age were employed, compared with approximately 5 in 10 disabled people and 8 in 10 non-disabled people.

The figures
The Buckland Review, published by the UK Government in February 2024, summarises that:
autistic people of working age were employed.
Comparison included in the report:

The Buckland Review compares employment among autistic people of working age with employment among disabled people overall and non-disabled people. It is a snapshot of the UK labour market using the latest data available to the review.
Cite ‘around 3 in 10’ and attribute it to the Buckland Review with the years of data available. Do not turn it into a global rate.
The report uses the latest official figures available at that time, mainly 2021/22 and 2022/23. Do not turn it into a ‘world autism employment rate’.
